intelligence.human_view: The weekday objects were already going to be real objects — obsidian in the middle, the day's color glowing around the outside (SN-3116). He is adding the second half of what makes an object feel real: an effect so it presents a lot better, and an icon that is unique to the day and means something. Sunday is the crown chakra, 963 — a crown. The icon is not decoration; it is what the day represents, made visible. That is the difference between seven matching buttons and seven objects that each mean something: the crown tells you what Sunday is before you read the letters. And the method is his: think of what the day represents first, then make the icon that is relevant to it — the meaning comes before the mark. He made the mock himself, quick, to show the shape — "you can probably do something even better" — which is the same discernment he asked for all hour: take the shape, make it better, don't paste it. The other six days' meanings are open work, not guessed: he named Sunday only, and the team must think through what Monday through Saturday represent before drawing their icons. A guessed icon would be decoration; a thought-through one is the day's meaning.
